### What is bookmarker?

bookmarker is a free bookmark manager for iPhone and the web that collects everything you
save on Instagram, X (Twitter), TikTok, YouTube and the open web into one library, files every save into a
topic automatically, and lets you find it again later. It is for people who save hundreds or thousands of
posts across several apps and can never find any of them again.

Every app keeps its own saved list. None of them talk to each other, almost nothing in them has a title
worth reading, and there is no subject to browse by — so you end up with five separate piles of things you
meant to come back to. bookmarker is the layer above all of them. A saved item is a bork.

### What it does

#### Save from anywhere

Tap Share in any iPhone app and pick bookmarker, or paste a link here on the web. The title, the
account that posted it and a thumbnail come along where the platform publishes them.

#### It files itself

Every bork lands in a topic and subtopic — Fitness › Mobility, Recipes › Meal prep. Fifty
topics, 612 subtopics, your own subtopics on top, and every suggestion is overridable. Keyword matching
does it on the spot and offline; signed in, the links it cannot place go to our server, which asks a
language model.

#### Browse two ways

By topic, to see everything about running wherever it came from. Or by source app, to see everything
you kept from TikTok. Each view filters the other.

#### Find it again

Search the title, the account, any post text that came with the save, your tags, your notes, the topic
and subtopic, the source app and the link — and narrow a search to topics, subtopics or tags when a word
is too common.

#### Notes, and a memory

Add a dated note so you remember why you kept something. bookmarker also counts how many times you
have gone back to it — the signal platform bookmarks throw away.

#### Bring what you already saved

Import your browser bookmarks, or the data export from X, Instagram, TikTok or YouTube, and thousands
of old saves become a filed, searchable library in one step.

### How it works

- Share. In Instagram, TikTok or YouTube, tap Share and pick bookmarker. On X, tap Share
and then “Share via…”. Pin bookmarker to the front of the share sheet once and it is the first icon from
then on.

- Bork. The link, the title, the account and a thumbnail are recorded on the spot.
Saving is one tap; organising is optional and can happen later.

- Filed. It lands in a topic and subtopic, ready to browse, search, annotate and open —
straight back to the original post in the app it came from.

### What it costs

bookmarker is free on the App Store, for iOS 17 or later. Your first 20 saves need no account at all. Past
20, signing up is also free — an email address and a six-digit code, no password to invent — and makes the
library unlimited, backs it up, and makes it readable here on the web. There is no paid tier in the app and
nothing in it costs money.

### Common questions

#### Which apps can I save from?

Any app with an iOS share sheet. bookmarker recognises Instagram, X (Twitter), TikTok, YouTube, YouTube
Shorts, Threads, Pinterest and ordinary web pages, and labels each save with where it came from.

#### Does bookmarker copy the posts I save?

No. It stores the link, the title, the account and a thumbnail where one is published, and opening a
save sends you to the original. It is not an archive: if the original is deleted, the link dies with it.

#### What exactly can I search?

Titles, accounts, tags, notes, topics, subtopics, the source app, the link, and whatever post text came
with the save — the description a page published, or the full post body when the save arrived in an X data
export. What bookmarker never does is open the page behind the link, so the body of an article, a PDF or a
video transcript is not indexed. There is no quoted-phrase operator either — several words mean “all of
these must appear”.

#### Will I get thumbnails for Instagram, TikTok and X?

Often not. YouTube and most web pages publish the metadata bookmarker reads; Instagram, TikTok and X
usually do not publish it to an unauthenticated request, so those saves often arrive with a plain title
and no image. The save, the filing and the search still work.

#### Is there an Android app?

No. There is an iPhone app and this web app, which runs in any modern browser — including on Android and
on a desktop — once you have signed in.

## What is bookmarker?

Last updated: 21 October 2026

bookmarker is a free bookmark manager for iPhone and the web that collects everything you save on
Instagram, X (Twitter), TikTok, YouTube and the open web into one library, files every save into a topic
automatically, and lets you find it again later. It is for people who save hundreds or thousands of posts
across several apps and can never find any of them again.

### The problem it solves

A reel on Instagram, a thread on X, a clip on TikTok, a recipe video on YouTube — every app keeps its own
saved list. None of those lists share anything with each other, almost none of the items have real titles, and
there is no topic to browse by. So you end up with five separate piles of things you meant to come back to, and
no way to answer the only question you ever actually ask: where did I see that thing about…?

bookmarker is the layer above all of them. One library, every app, filed and searchable.

### What it does

- Saves from anywhere. Tap Share in any iPhone app and pick bookmarker, or paste a link into
the app, or paste it into the web app at bookmarker.lol.

- Files itself. Every save lands in a topic and a subtopic — Fitness › Mobility,
Recipes › Meal prep. There are 50 topics and 612 subtopics, and you can add your own subtopics. The
filing is a suggestion: you can change it before or after saving.

- Browses two ways. By topic, to see everything about running wherever it came from; or by
source app, to see everything you kept from TikTok. Each view filters the other.

- Finds things again. Search covers the title, the account that posted it, your tags, your
notes, the topic and subtopic, the source app and the link itself. You can narrow a search to topics,
subtopics or tags only.

- Remembers why. Add a dated note to any save, and bookmarker counts how often you have
gone back to something — the signal platform bookmarks throw away.

- Imports what you already saved. Browser bookmarks, or the data export from X, Instagram,
TikTok or YouTube. Thousands of old saves become a filed, searchable library in one step.

- Shares a set. Pick some saves and bookmarker turns them into a page at
bookmarker.lol/c/… that you can send to anyone, with an expiry of never, one day or ten days, and a
switch to turn it off.

### Who it is for

- Heavy savers — people with hundreds or thousands of likes and bookmarks across Instagram, X, TikTok and YouTube.

- People who save practical things: recipes, workouts, product research, travel itineraries, tutorials.

- Anyone who has thought "I definitely saved that" and then failed to find it.

- People who want their library on their own phone rather than in another company's feed.

### What it does not do

Being specific here is more useful than overselling:

- It stores links, not copies. bookmarker keeps the link, the title, the account and a
thumbnail where one is published. Opening a save sends you to the original post in the app it came from. It
is not an archive — if the original is deleted, the link dies with it.

- Thumbnails and titles are only as good as the platform allows. YouTube and most ordinary
web pages publish the metadata bookmarker needs. Instagram, TikTok and X usually do not publish it to an
unauthenticated request, so saves from those apps often arrive with a plain title and no image.

- Search does not reach into the page behind the link. It matches what bookmarker holds:
titles, accounts, tags, notes, topics, source and link, plus whatever post text came with the save — the
description a page published, or the full post body when it arrived in an X data export. Nothing fetches the
body of an article, a PDF or a video transcript, so none of that is indexed. There is no quoted-phrase
operator — multiple words are treated as "all of these must appear".

- No Android app. There is an iPhone app and a web app that runs in any modern browser.

- Filing is keyword-first; a language model is the backup, not the engine. The pass that
runs on your device is a keyword score, so it does well on descriptive links and captions and leaves an
opaque link unfiled rather than guessing. When you are signed in, those leftovers go to our server, which
asks a language model — so filing is only entirely on-device when you are signed out.

### What it costs

bookmarker is free on the App Store. Your first 20 saves work with no account at all. Past 20, saving asks
you to sign up — that is also free, an email address and a six-digit code — and signing up makes the library
unlimited, backs it up, and makes it readable on the web. There is no paid tier in the app and nothing in it
costs money. A one-time founding-member price of $30 is being reserved for a future
paid version; payments are not switched on, and no card is taken.

### Where to go next

#### The iPhone app →
Screens, the share sheet flow, import, privacy.

#### FAQ →
Fifteen straight answers about accounts, search, privacy and limits.

#### Alternatives →
An honest look at the other tools in this category.

The problem

### Saved everywhere. Findable nowhere.

A reel on Instagram, a thread on X, a clip on TikTok, a video on YouTube — every app keeps its own saved list. None of them are titled, sorted or searchable, so you never find any of it again.

bork noun, verb

A saved item. You bork something. Then you can search it, file it, and open the original.

“412 borks.” That’s the product.

What it does

### One library above all of them.

Saving is instant. Organising is optional — bookmarker does most of it for you, and you can change anything it gets wrong.

#### Save from anywhere

Tap Share in any app and pick bookmarker, or paste a link. The title, the account that posted it and a thumbnail come along automatically. Pin bookmarker to the front of your share sheet once (More → Edit → add to Favorites) and it's the first icon every time.

#### It files itself

Every bork lands in a topic and subtopic — Fitness › Mobility, Recipes › Meal prep. Fifty topics, six hundred subtopics, and you can add your own.

#### Browse two ways

By topic, to see everything about running no matter where it came from. Or by app, to see everything you kept from TikTok. Each view filters the other.

#### Find it again

Search titles, tags, notes, people and links. A Related strip surfaces the near-matches — what you meant, not just the words you typed.

#### Notes, and a memory

Add a dated note to any bork so you remember why you kept it. bookmarker also counts how many times you’ve gone back to it.

#### Side quests

Running a marathon, choosing a car, planning a trip? Group the links that help with the goal, and add a daily habit if it needs one.

How it works

### Share. Bork. Filed.

STEP 1

#### Share

Tap Share in Instagram, TikTok, YouTube — anywhere — and pick bookmarker (on X, tap Share, then Share via…). Pin it once — scroll the app icons to More, tap Edit, add bookmarker to Favorites and drag it to the front — and it's the first icon from then on. Or paste a link straight into the app.

STEP 2

#### bookmarker

The title, who posted it and a thumbnail are fetched on the spot. Saving takes one tap; organising is optional and can happen later.

STEP 3

#### Filed

It lands in a topic and subtopic, ready to browse, search and open — straight back to the original post in the app it came from.

Import

### Bring what you already saved.

## bookmarker FAQ

Last updated: 21 October 2026

Straight answers about bookmarker — the free bookmark manager for iPhone and the web that puts
everything you save on Instagram, X, TikTok and YouTube into one searchable library. If something you need is
not here, email hello@bookmarker.lol.

### What is bookmarker?

bookmarker is a free bookmark manager for iPhone and the web. It collects everything you save on
Instagram, X (Twitter), TikTok, YouTube and the open web into one library, files each save into a topic and
subtopic automatically, and lets you search it later. A saved item is called a bork.

### Who is bookmarker for?

People who save a lot and lose it: hundreds or thousands of reels, threads, clips and articles spread
across four or five apps, none of them searchable. If you have ever thought "I definitely saved that" and
failed to find it, that is the audience.

### How much does bookmarker cost?

It is free on the App Store. The first 20 saves need no account. Past 20, saving asks you to sign up,
which is also free — an email address and a six-digit code — and makes the library unlimited, backed up and
readable on the web. There is no paid tier in the app and nothing in it costs money. A one-time
founding-member price of $30 is being reserved for a future paid version; payments are
not switched on yet and no card is taken.

### Which apps can I save from?

Any app with an iOS share sheet. bookmarker recognises Instagram, X (Twitter), TikTok, YouTube, YouTube
Shorts, Threads, Pinterest and ordinary web pages, and labels each save with where it came from. On X, tap
Share and then "Share via…" to reach the share sheet. You can also paste a link straight into the app
or into the web app.

### Do I need an account?

Not to start. Everything works signed out for your first 20 saves, offline, on your phone. Signing in is
free and does three things: removes the 20-save limit, backs the library up, and lets you open it on the web.
There is no password to invent — you get a six-digit code by email.

### How does the automatic filing work?

In two passes. The first scores the words in the link and the title or caption against the topic list and
files the save into the best of 50 topics and 612 subtopics — you can add your own subtopics too. That pass
runs on your device, instantly and offline, and it settles most links.

It is keyword matching, so an opaque link ("she does this every morning and it changed my skin") comes back
with nothing rather than a wild guess. For those leftovers — and only when you are signed in —
bookmarker sends the link, its title or caption, the account, the hashtags and any tags you typed to its own
server, which asks a language model where the save belongs. Answers the model is not confident about are
thrown away rather than shown. Signed out, offline, or if that request fails, you keep the offline answer; your
notes are never sent. The privacy policy sets this out in full.

Either way the topic is a suggestion you can override, and saving is never blocked by filing.

### What exactly can I search?

By default a search looks at the title, the account that posted it, your tags, your notes, the topic and
subtopic, the source app, the link itself, and whatever post text bookmarker holds — the description a
page published, or the full post body when the save came in from an X data export. You can narrow a search to
topics, subtopics or tags only. Several words are treated as "all of these must appear somewhere"; there is no
quoted-phrase or operator syntax.

What it does not promise is the whole document behind the link. bookmarker never fetches the body of an
article, a PDF or a video transcript, so a phrase that appears only deep inside the thing you saved will not
be found.

### Does bookmarker work offline?

Yes. The iPhone library lives on your iPhone, and browsing, searching, saving a pasted link and the keyword
filing all work with no connection. Fetching a title or a thumbnail needs the network, as does the model that
files the links keyword matching cannot place, so those parts fill in when you are back online.

### Does bookmarker copy the posts I save?

No. It stores the link, the title, the account and a thumbnail where the platform publishes one. Opening
a save sends you to the original post in the app it came from. That means bookmarker is not an archive: if the
original is deleted, the link stops working.

### Will I get thumbnails for Instagram, TikTok and X saves?

Often not, and it is worth being straight about why. YouTube and most ordinary web pages publish the
title, author and image that bookmarker reads. Instagram, TikTok and X generally do not publish that metadata
to an unauthenticated request, so saves from those apps frequently arrive with a plain title taken from the
share sheet caption or the link, and no image. The save, the filing and the search all still work.

### Can I import the saves I already have?

Yes. bookmarker imports browser bookmarks and the data export files from X, Instagram, TikTok and
YouTube. Every platform is obliged to hand your data over, so a few thousand old saves can become a filed,
searchable library in one pass instead of being re-saved one at a time.

### What happens if I save the same link twice?

You get one bork, not two. bookmarker normalises every URL before storing it — lowercases the host,
strips www. and m., drops tracking parameters such as utm_*,
igshid, si and fbclid, and removes trailing slashes — so the same post
shared from two places, or shared once and pasted once, collides into a single save.

### Can I share my saves with someone?

Yes. Pick a set of saves and bookmarker turns them into a page at bookmarker.lol/c/…
you can send to anyone, no account needed to read it. You choose whether the link lasts forever, one day or
ten days, and you can switch it off afterwards. Everything else in your library stays private.

### Is there an Android or desktop app?

There is no Android app. There is a native iPhone app (iOS 17 or later) and a web app at
bookmarker.lol that runs in any modern browser, including on Android and on a desktop, once
you have signed in.

### Does bookmarker track me?

The iPhone app asks for zero permissions and ships with no ad or analytics SDKs; your library is on your
device. This website uses PostHog for product analytics and session replay with inputs masked, which the
privacy policy discloses. Your saves are never sold and are not visible to anyone else
unless you deliberately share a collection.

Get bookmarker — free

Free on the App Store, iOS 17 or later. See also
what bookmarker is, the
alternatives, and how it compares to X bookmarks.

## Best bookmark managers for saved posts and X bookmarks

Last updated: 21 October 2026 · written by the team that makes bookmarker

If you save a lot on X, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube and can never find any of it again, there
are about five serious options, and they are built for genuinely different jobs. This page says what each one is
for, where it beats the others, and which parts of the problem it does not touch. We make
bookmarker, so treat the summary of our own product as the one you should
check hardest.

Competitor details below are from each product's own website, checked on
21 October 2026, and they change. Follow the links and confirm anything that matters to you. Where a rival is
better at something, it says so.

### The short version

Tool
Built for
Where it is strongest

bookmarker

Saves from several phone apps at once

One library across Instagram, X, TikTok and YouTube; automatic topic filing; saving from the iOS share sheet; free

Raindrop.io

Web pages, articles and research

Runs on everything, browser extensions, full-text search of saved page content, archived copies, sharing and teamwork

Twillot

X (Twitter) only, in a desktop browser

Pulling your whole X bookmark, like and post history down into a local archive, with export

mymind

Visual inspiration and notes

Beautiful visual library, AI organising so you need not file anything, strong privacy stance, iPhone + Android + extensions

Built-in bookmarks (X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube)

Saving one thing in the app you are already in

Zero friction, nothing to install, free

### bookmarker

What it is: a free bookmark manager for iPhone and the web that collects everything you save
across apps into one library and files each save into a topic and subtopic automatically — 50 topics, 612
subtopics. You save with the iOS share sheet, by pasting a link, or by importing your X, Instagram, TikTok,
YouTube or browser-bookmark export. You can then browse by topic or by source app, search, add dated notes, and
share a set of saves as a link.

Strongest at: the cross-app problem. It is the only tool here whose whole premise is that
your Instagram reel and your X thread about the same marathon belong in the same place. Filing is automatic, so
a library of a few thousand saves is usable without you organising anything.

Weakest at: depth per platform and depth per page. It stores links, not copies, so it cannot
show you a post that has been deleted, and search covers only the text that came with a save — never the article,
PDF or transcript behind the link. Thumbnails and titles are frequently missing for Instagram, TikTok and X saves
because those platforms do not publish metadata to unauthenticated requests. There is no Android app and no
browser extension, though the web app runs in an Android or desktop browser. It cannot reach into X and pull your
existing bookmark list down — for that you import X's data export.

Price: free on the App Store; first 20 saves with no account, then a free email sign-in for
an unlimited, backed-up library. Full FAQ.

### Raindrop.io

What it is: a mature, all-purpose bookmark manager. Per raindrop.io, it runs as a web app,
browser extensions and apps across platforms, and organises saves into nestable collections with tags and
filters. It also offers highlights and annotations, duplicate and broken-link detection, several view modes,
integrations, archived copies of saved pages, and full-text search across the content of saved pages, PDFs and
YouTube videos.

Stronger than bookmarker at: almost everything to do with web pages. If what you save is
mostly articles and research, Raindrop is the better tool — real full-text search inside saved content, and a
permanent archived copy so a dead link still has something behind it. Raindrop also offers native Android and
desktop apps and browser extensions; bookmarker offers an iPhone app and a web app usable in desktop and Android
browsers.

Where bookmarker differs: Raindrop is browser-first and you choose the collection; bookmarker
is phone-share-sheet-first and files every save into a topic for you. If your saving happens inside Instagram and
TikTok rather than in a browser, that difference matters more than the feature lists do.

Full comparison: bookmarker vs Raindrop.io →

### Twillot

What it is: per twillot.com, a browser extension that turns your X (Twitter) bookmarks into a
searchable library — it syncs your bookmarks, likes, posts and replies into an archive held in your browser, with
folders, AI organising, search, media downloads and export, and it keeps posts after they are deleted.

Stronger than bookmarker at: X, by a wide margin. It reaches your existing X bookmark history
directly instead of asking you to import a data export, it keeps copies so deleted posts survive, and it exports
your archive. If your problem is specifically "I have 4,000 X bookmarks", start there.

Where bookmarker differs: Twillot is X-only and lives in a desktop browser. bookmarker covers
Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and the open web as well, and works from the phone you were already holding.

Full comparison: bookmarker vs Twillot →

### mymind

What it is: per mymind.com, a private visual library for notes, bookmarks, inspiration,
articles and images — "remember everything, organize nothing". You save with a click and its AI handles the
organising, so its home page says you need not file, label or even tag anything. Organising is optional rather
than absent: mymind's own guide to Spaces describes adding your own tags, saving a search as a Smart Space that
fills itself, and right-clicking an item to add it to a Space by hand. It has iPhone and Android apps plus
Chrome, Edge and Safari extensions, and explicitly has no social features, no collaboration and no ads.

Stronger than bookmarker at: visual material and craft. If you are collecting images,
palettes, type and product shots, mymind's visual library is a nicer place to look at them than a list of links,
and it has a native Android app and browser extensions where bookmarker has neither.

Where bookmarker differs: bookmarker leads with the structure — a visible topic tree you
browse and reassign, with the source app as a dimension of its own — where mymind leads with search over a
library that organised itself. bookmarker is built around posts from social apps, and it is free.

Full comparison: bookmarker vs mymind →

### The bookmarks built into X, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube

What they are: free, instant, and already on your phone. For saving one thing you will look at
tomorrow, nothing beats them.

Where they stop: each one is a separate list inside a separate app, so what you save is split
four or five ways. Most of them show you no title worth reading, no topic to browse by, and no record of what you
have actually gone back to. Feature availability varies and changes — X, for instance, has added bookmark folders
for subscribers — so check the current help pages of each app rather than trusting an older comparison.

Full comparison: bookmarker vs X bookmarks →

### What about Pocket and Instapaper?

Pocket, the best-known read-it-later app, has shut down: Mozilla's notice on getpocket.com says the Pocket web,
Android, iOS and macOS apps and the browser extensions have been phased out, so it is no longer an option.
Instapaper is still a good
read-later app for long articles, but it is built for reading text, not for keeping track of reels, clips and
threads — which is the problem this page is about.

### How to choose

- Most of what you save is in phone apps, across several of them → bookmarker.

- Most of what you save is web articles and research → Raindrop.io.

- You only care about X, and you want your existing bookmark history → Twillot.

- You collect images, want it to look beautiful, or need Android or a browser extension → mymind.

- You save a handful of things a month → the built-in bookmarks are fine.

Plenty of people run two: a web-first manager for articles and bookmarker for everything the phone throws at
them. The workflows barely overlap.

Try bookmarker — free

Free on the App Store, iOS 17 or later, or in a browser at bookmarker.lol.

bookmarker › bookmarker vs X bookmarks

## bookmarker vs X (Twitter) built-in bookmarks

Last updated: 21 October 2026

X has a bookmark button, it is free, and it is one tap. So why add anything? The short answer:
X's bookmarks only ever hold X, and they tell you nothing about what you saved or whether you ever went back to
it. bookmarker is a free iPhone and web library that holds your X saves and your Instagram, TikTok and
YouTube saves, files each one into a topic, and lets you search and annotate the lot.

X's bookmark features change, and some of them depend on a paid X Premium tier — bookmark
folders, for instance, have been a subscriber feature. Check X's current help pages rather than trusting any
comparison, including this one, on the detail. Everything below is about what a separate library adds, which does
not change.

### What X's built-in bookmarks are good at

Zero friction. You are already in X, you tap the bookmark icon, it is saved, there is nothing to install and
nothing to pay. For something you intend to read tomorrow, nothing is better. If you save a handful of posts a
month and only use X, you do not need anything else — and this page is not going to pretend otherwise.

### What they cannot do

#### 1. They only hold X

This is the big one. Your Instagram saves, TikTok favourites and YouTube "Watch later" are three more separate
lists in three more apps. Nothing in X's bookmarks can see them, so the recipe you saved on Instagram and the
recipe thread you saved on X never sit next to each other.

#### 2. There is no topic to browse by

X's bookmarks are a reverse-chronological list. You cannot ask for "just the coding threads" or "just the
recipes" unless you have manually filed things into folders — and folders are a paid-tier feature and still
manual. You remember what something was about, not when you saved it.

#### 3. They do not tell you what you actually use

No dates to sort by, no note about why you kept it, and no record of how many times you have gone back to
something. The platform has no reason to build that: its business is your next scroll, not your last one.

#### 4. They stay inside X

You cannot send someone a curated set of twenty saved posts as one link, and you cannot keep a copy anywhere
you control.

### What bookmarker adds

- One library across apps. X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, YouTube Shorts, Threads, Pinterest
and ordinary web pages, each labelled with where it came from. Browse by topic or by source app; each view
filters the other.

- Automatic filing. Every save lands in a topic and subtopic — 50 topics, 612 subtopics,
always overridable, and you can add your own subtopics.

- Search. Over titles, the account that posted it, any post text that came with the save,
your tags, your notes, the topic and subtopic, the source app and the link, narrowable to topics, subtopics
or tags.

- Dated notes. Why you kept it, written down, with a date.

- Revisit counts. bookmarker counts how often you reopen a save, so the things you actually
use rise to the top.

- Shareable collections. Turn a set of saves into a page at bookmarker.lol/c/… with an
expiry of never, one day or ten days, and switch it off whenever.

- Your old saves. Import X's data export, plus Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and browser
bookmarks.

- It is free. First 20 saves with no account; a free email sign-in makes it unlimited and
backed up.

One thing to be clear about, because it is easy to oversell: bookmarker searches what it
holds, not the page behind the link. A search matches the title, the account that posted it, your tags, your
notes, the topic and subtopic, the source app, the link, and whatever post text came with the save — the
description a page published, or the full post body when the save arrived in an X data export. What is never
fetched, and so never searchable, is the rest of the document: the body of an article, a PDF, a video
transcript. You can narrow a search to topics, subtopics or tags. Several words mean "all of these must appear";
there is no quoted-phrase operator.

bookmarker also stores links rather than copies, so it does not rescue a deleted post — if that is what you
need, look at Twillot, which archives X posts.

### When X's bookmarks are enough

- You save a handful of posts and clear them out regularly.

- X is the only app you save from.

- You do not need to search or group what you saved.

### When a separate library is worth it

- You have hundreds or thousands of saves and find nothing.

- You save from Instagram, TikTok and YouTube as well.

- You want to browse by subject rather than scroll by date.

- You want to know what you keep coming back to, or to send someone a set.

Plenty of people use both: X's bookmarks as a quick inbox, bookmarker for anything they want to keep.

## bookmarker vs Raindrop.io

Last updated: 21 October 2026

Both are bookmark managers, and they are built for different halves of the problem.
Raindrop.io is a mature, cross-platform
manager for web pages, articles and research that you save from a browser. bookmarker is a free iPhone and web
library for the posts you save inside Instagram, X, TikTok and YouTube, filed into topics automatically. If your
saving happens in a browser, Raindrop is probably the better answer; if it happens in phone apps, bookmarker is.

Competitor details here come from the other product's own website, checked on
21 October 2026, and they change. Follow the links and confirm anything that matters to you. Where the other
tool is better, it says so.

### What Raindrop.io does, in its own terms

Per raindrop.io, Raindrop runs as a web app, browser extensions and apps across platforms, and organises saves
into nestable collections with tags and filters. It finds duplicates and broken links, offers highlights and
annotations, several view modes (grid, headlines, masonry, list), integrations and an API, sharing and permissions
for collaborators, and backups to Dropbox or Google Drive. Two things stand out as genuinely strong: it keeps an
archived copy of saved web pages, so a page that is taken down still has something behind it; and its full-text
search covers the entire content of every saved page, PDF and YouTube video, not just titles and tags. It has a
free plan and a paid subscription.

### What bookmarker does

bookmarker starts from the phone. You tap Share in any app and pick bookmarker, or paste a link, or import the
data export from X, Instagram, TikTok or YouTube. Every save lands in a topic and subtopic automatically — 50
topics, 612 subtopics, all overridable — and the app it came from is recorded, so you can browse by topic
("everything about running, wherever it came from") or by source ("everything I kept from TikTok"), with each
filtering the other. You can add a dated note to any save, bookmarker counts how often you reopen something, and
you can turn a set of saves into a shareable page at bookmarker.lol/c/… with an optional expiry.

### Where Raindrop.io is better

- Search depth. Raindrop indexes the whole content of a saved page, PDF or YouTube video.
bookmarker searches only the text that arrived with the save — see the note below.

- Archiving. Raindrop keeps copies of saved pages. bookmarker stores links only, so a deleted
post is simply gone.

- Platform coverage. Raindrop has browser extensions and runs on Android, Windows and macOS.
bookmarker is an iPhone app plus a web app, with no browser extension and no Android app.

- Manual structure and teamwork. Nestable collections, permissions, shared editing, an API.

- Maturity. It has been around far longer and has the feature surface to show for it.

One thing to be clear about, because it is easy to oversell: bookmarker searches what it
holds, not the page behind the link. A search matches the title, the account that posted it, your tags, your
notes, the topic and subtopic, the source app, the link, and whatever post text came with the save — the
description a page published, or the full post body when the save arrived in an X data export. What is never
fetched, and so never searchable, is the rest of the document: the body of an article, a PDF, a video
transcript. You can narrow a search to topics, subtopics or tags. Several words mean "all of these must appear";
there is no quoted-phrase operator.

### Where bookmarker is better

- Saving from social apps. bookmarker is designed for the share sheet inside Instagram,
TikTok, YouTube and X, and it labels every save with the app it came from.

- Filing you do not have to do. Raindrop asks which collection; bookmarker picks a topic and
subtopic and lets you correct it. With a few thousand saves, that difference is the whole product.

- Two browse axes that cross. Topic and source app, each filtering the other.

- Dated notes and revisit counts. Why you kept something, and whether you ever went back.

- Price. bookmarker is free, including the unlimited, backed-up library after a free email
sign-in.

### Can you use both?

Yes, and it is a sensible setup: Raindrop for articles and research you save in a browser, bookmarker for the
reels, clips and threads you save on your phone. The workflows barely touch — one is browser-first, the other is
share-sheet-first.

### The bottom line

Choose Raindrop.io if most of what you keep is web pages, you want them searchable to the word and archived,
and you need Android, Windows or a browser extension. Choose bookmarker if most of what you keep is posts from
social apps, you want them filed by topic without doing it yourself, and you want it free.

## bookmarker vs Twillot

Last updated: 21 October 2026

Both tools exist because X's bookmark list becomes useless once it is long. They attack it from
opposite ends. Twillot is a
browser extension that reaches into X and pulls your entire bookmark, like and post history down into a local
archive. bookmarker is a free iPhone and web library that takes new saves from any app — X, Instagram,
TikTok, YouTube — and files them into topics. If your problem is "I already have 4,000 X bookmarks", Twillot is
the more direct answer.

Competitor details here come from the other product's own website, checked on
21 October 2026, and they change. Follow the links and confirm anything that matters to you. Where the other
tool is better, it says so.

### What Twillot does, in its own terms

Per twillot.com, Twillot turns your X bookmarks into a searchable library: it syncs your bookmarks, likes,
posts and replies, gets you past X's scroll limit to reach your full history, keeps the data inside your browser,
and preserves posts even after they are deleted. Its listed features include search, "folders that fill
themselves", AI organising, export of your archive, an offline archive and media downloads. It is a browser
extension with a web workspace, and it has a free start plus paid plans.

### What bookmarker does

bookmarker is a native iPhone app (iOS 17+) with a web app. You save by tapping Share in any app and picking
bookmarker — on X, tap Share and then "Share via…" — or by pasting a link, or by importing the data export
from X, Instagram, TikTok or YouTube. Every save is filed into one of 50 topics and 612 subtopics automatically
and overridably, labelled with the app it came from, and browsable either way. You can add dated notes, see how
often you have reopened something, and share a set of saves as a link with an optional expiry.

### Where Twillot is better

- Getting your existing X bookmarks. Twillot syncs them directly from X. bookmarker cannot
read your X bookmark list — you import X's data export instead, which means requesting the archive and
waiting for it.

- Surviving deletion. Twillot says it preserves posts after they are deleted. bookmarker
stores links, so a deleted post is gone.

- Export and bulk operations. Exporting your archive and downloading media are headline
Twillot features.

- Desktop. It lives in a desktop browser, which is where a lot of people do their reading.

- X depth generally. Likes, replies and your own posts, not just bookmarks.

### Where bookmarker is better

- It is not only X. Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, YouTube Shorts, Threads, Pinterest and plain
web pages all land in the same library, with the source app recorded.

- It works where you actually see the post. You are holding a phone in Instagram; a desktop
browser extension cannot help there.

- Browse by topic across sources. Your X thread and your Instagram reel about the same
marathon end up in the same topic.

- Dated notes and revisit counts.

- Price. bookmarker is free, including the unlimited backed-up library after a free email
sign-in.

One thing to be clear about, because it is easy to oversell: bookmarker searches what it
holds, not the page behind the link. A search matches the title, the account that posted it, your tags, your
notes, the topic and subtopic, the source app, the link, and whatever post text came with the save — the
description a page published, or the full post body when the save arrived in an X data export. What is never
fetched, and so never searchable, is the rest of the document: the body of an article, a PDF, a video
transcript. You can narrow a search to topics, subtopics or tags. Several words mean "all of these must appear";
there is no quoted-phrase operator.

already have, bookmarker for everything you save from now on, across every app.

### The bottom line

Twillot is the specialist — the right tool if the job is "get my X bookmarks out of X and keep them". bookmarker
is the generalist — the right tool if the job is "stop having five separate piles of saved posts on my phone".

bookmarker › bookmarker vs mymind

## bookmarker vs mymind

Last updated: 21 October 2026

bookmarker and mymind start from the same good idea — you should not have to file the things you
save — and then build two different products on it. bookmarker is a free iPhone and web library for posts you
save out of Instagram, X, TikTok and YouTube, filed into a visible topic tree. mymind is a paid, private visual
library for notes, bookmarks, images and inspiration, organised by AI with your own tags and Spaces available on
top if you want them.

Competitor details below are from each product's own website, checked on
21 October 2026, and they change. Follow the links and confirm anything that matters to you. Where a rival is
better at something, it says so.

### The core difference

mymind (per mymind.com) is "the extension for your mind": save anything with a click and its
AI takes care of the rest, so you need not file, label or even tag it. That is a promise about effort, not a
missing feature — mymind's guide to Spaces describes adding your own tags, turning a search into a Smart Space
that keeps filling itself, and adding an item to a Space by hand. Its emphasis is search over structure
("folders are dead; this is your personal search engine"). It is deliberately private — their site lists no
social features, no vanity metrics, no collaboration and no ads — and it leans visual, so a saved image, colour
or product shot is something you look at rather than a row in a list.

bookmarker is about the pile of posts you already have in five different apps. It files every
save into one of 50 topics and 612 subtopics, and it keeps the source app as a first-class dimension, so you can
ask for "everything about running" or "everything I kept from TikTok" and get a straight answer. The filing is
visible and editable rather than implicit.

### Where each one wins

#### mymind is better if…

- You collect visual material — images, type, palettes, products — and want a library that looks good.

- You want notes, highlights and bookmarks in the same place rather than links alone.

- You want a native Android app or a browser extension: mymind lists iPhone and Android apps plus Chrome,
Edge and Safari extensions. bookmarker has neither — its web app does run in an Android or desktop browser,
but there is nothing to install.

- You would rather search than browse a structure, and never see a category unless you ask for one.

#### bookmarker is better if…

- What you save comes out of social apps on a phone, and you want the app it came from recorded and filterable.

- You want to see and correct the filing — browse a topic tree, move a save, add your own subtopic.

- You already have thousands of saves to bring over: bookmarker imports browser bookmarks and the X,
Instagram, TikTok and YouTube data exports.

- You want the thing to be free.

### Side by side

### Can you use both?

Easily, because they collect different things. mymind for the visual scrapbook, bookmarker for the stream of
posts your phone throws at you. Neither one tries to be the other.

### The bottom line

Pick mymind if you are building a beautiful, private collection of things you want to look at, and you would
rather search it than navigate it. Pick bookmarker if your problem is thousands of saved posts scattered across
Instagram, X, TikTok and YouTube, and you want them in one free library with a topic tree you can browse and
correct.

bookmarker › How to organise your X bookmarks

## How to organise your X (Twitter) bookmarks

Last updated: 21 October 2026

If you have saved hundreds of posts on X and cannot find any of them, the problem is not you —
it is that a reverse-chronological list with no titles and no subjects is not an organisational system. This page
covers the realistic options, and then the method we think works: let something file each save into a topic as it
arrives, instead of trying to tidy the pile later.

X's own bookmark features change, and some of them (folders, for example) have
been limited to paid X Premium tiers. Check X's current help pages before assuming what your account can do. The
method below does not depend on which tier you are on.

### Why the bookmark list goes bad

Three things compound. The list is ordered by when you saved, but you remember what something was
about. Nothing in it has a useful title, so scanning does not work. And it only holds X, so the other
half of what you saved on the same subject is sitting in Instagram or YouTube where this list cannot see it. A
hundred saves is browsable. A thousand is a landfill.

### Your options, honestly

#### Manual folders inside X

If your account has bookmark folders, they work, and for a small number of broad buckets they are the least
effort. The catch is that they are manual, they only cover X, and every new save is a decision you have to make.

#### Copy posts into a notes app

Screenshotting into Apple Notes, Notion or Obsidian gives you full control and good search of your own words.
It is also slow, and you lose the live link back to the post, the replies and the author.

#### Export to a spreadsheet

You can request your X archive and search the bookmarks file in a spreadsheet. It is a snapshot — it does not
update, and it is unusable on a phone.

#### A library that files saves for you

The option with the least ongoing effort: save through a tool that assigns a subject at save time, so the
organising has already happened by the time you want to find something. That is what bookmarker does, and it is
the method below.

### The method, step by step

- Get bookmarker. Install bookmarker free from the App Store (iOS 17 or later), or open the web app at bookmarker.lol. Your first 20 saves work with no account.

- Save a post from X. In X, tap Share on the post, then “Share via…” to reach the iOS share sheet, and pick bookmarker. Pin bookmarker to the front of the share sheet once — More → Edit → add to Favourites — and it is the first icon from then on.

- Let it file the save. bookmarker scores the words in the link and the title or caption against its topic list and files the save into a topic and subtopic, such as Fitness › Mobility. Change it there and then if it guessed wrong; saving is never blocked by filing.

- Bring your existing bookmarks in. Request your X data archive (X Settings → Your account → Download an archive of your data), then import the file into bookmarker so your old saves are filed too.

- Browse by topic instead of scrolling. Open Browse and pick a topic to see everything on that subject from every app, or switch the axis to browse by source app. Add tags for one-off projects, and a dated note when you want to remember why you kept something.

### Why topics beat folders

Folders are a decision per save. Topics are a decision you never make: bookmarker picks one of 50 topics and
612 subtopics from the words in the link and the caption, and you only intervene when it is wrong. With a couple
of thousand saves that is the difference between a system you keep up with and one you abandon in week two.

The pass that does the work is keyword matching against the topic list, which runs on your device, instantly
and offline. That has one honest consequence: it is good on descriptive links and captions, and it deliberately
leaves a save unfiled rather than guessing wildly when a link is opaque. X links are often opaque, so expect to
correct some of them — it takes one tap, and corrections stick. When you are signed in, the links keyword
matching could not place are sent on to bookmarker's server, which asks a language model where they belong and
discards answers it is not confident about; signed out or offline, the keyword answer is the only answer.

### Tags for the things topics cannot know

Topics handle subjects. Tags handle projects: tag everything you save for a specific conference, trip or client
and pull the set back instantly. A dated note on a save is for the other half of the problem — remembering
why you kept it.

### Organise across apps, not just X

The point of all this only lands when the library holds more than X. Your Instagram recipe reel and your X
recipe thread belong in the same place, and in bookmarker they are both in Recipes, each still labelled with the
app it came from, so you can filter by source when you want to.

### What this will not fix

bookmarker stores links, not copies: if a post is deleted, the link dies. And many X saves arrive with a plain
title and no thumbnail, because X does not publish that metadata to unauthenticated requests. The filing, the
notes and the search all still work; the card just looks plainer than a YouTube one.

## How to search your X (Twitter) bookmarks

Last updated: 21 October 2026

Saved a good post weeks ago and cannot find it? The reason is that X's search box searches X, not
your saves, and scrolling a long bookmark list is not searching. This page covers the two methods that actually
work — exporting your archive, and keeping saves in a library built to be searched — and is specific about what
each one can and cannot match.

X's own bookmark features change, and some of them (folders, for example) have
been limited to paid X Premium tiers. Check X's current help pages before assuming what your account can do. The
method below does not depend on which tier you are on.

### Why scrolling fails

A bookmark list is ordered by when you saved. You remember what something was about, who posted it, or roughly
what it looked like — almost never the date. So the one axis the list gives you is the one axis you cannot use,
and with a few hundred saves the only honest strategy left is luck.

### Method 1: export your X archive and search the file

- Open X → Settings → Your account → Download an archive of your data.

- Wait for X to prepare it — this can take a day.

- Download the archive and unzip it.

- Open the bookmarks data file and search it in a spreadsheet or text editor.

What it is good for: a one-off hunt, and it costs nothing. What it is bad for:
it is a snapshot that never updates, it is awkward on a phone, and you have to re-export to catch anything new.

### Method 2: keep your saves in a library you can search

The method with no maintenance: save through something that records the useful fields at save time, so finding
is a search rather than an excavation. bookmarker is free, works from the X share sheet, and holds your Instagram,
TikTok and YouTube saves in the same place.

- Get bookmarker. Install bookmarker free from the App Store (iOS 17 or later) or open the web app at bookmarker.lol.

- Save X posts through it. In X, tap Share, then “Share via…”, then bookmarker. The link, the title where X publishes one, the account and the source app are recorded, and the save is filed into a topic.

- Import the bookmarks you already have. Request your X archive under X Settings → Your account → Download an archive of your data, then import the file so your existing saves become searchable too.

- Search your library. Type a word into the search field. bookmarker matches the title, the account that posted it, your tags, your notes, the topic and subtopic, the source app, the link, and any description text the page published.

- Narrow it when a word is too common. Tap the Topics, Subtopics or Tags chips to restrict a search to those fields, or filter the results by source app to see only X.

### Exactly what bookmarker's search matches

Worth spelling out, because "full-text search" gets claimed loosely in this category. A bookmarker search looks
at:

- the title of the save;

- the account or handle that posted it;

- your tags;

- your notes;

- the topic and subtopic it was filed into;

- the source app;

- the link itself;

- and whatever post text bookmarker holds — the description a page published, which Instagram, TikTok and X
usually do not provide, or the full post body when the save arrived in an X data export.

What it does not do is open the page behind the link. The body of an article, a PDF or a
video transcript is never fetched, so none of it is searchable, and there is no quoted-phrase or operator syntax:
typing several words means "every one of these must appear somewhere". If you need search that reaches inside
saved page content, Raindrop.io does that and we say so on the comparison page. If you
want a full, lasting copy of your X posts rather than the text an export happens to carry,
Twillot archives them.

### Getting more out of a search

#### Search the word you would use for the subject

Because every save is filed into a topic and subtopic, the subject word usually hits even when the title is
useless — searching "mobility" finds things filed under Fitness › Mobility whose titles never said it.

#### Scope the search when a word is everywhere

A query like "running" matches eleven titles as loudly as the topic you actually filed things under. Tapping
the Topics, Subtopics or Tags chips restricts the match to those fields, which is usually the fix.

#### Filter by the app it came from

If you know you saved it on X, filter the results by source and the list collapses to a handful.

#### Give future-you something to search for

A tag or a one-line dated note at save time is the single highest-leverage habit here — those are your words,
so they are the words you will search for.

### Why author search is not the answer

Searching X for the person who posted it only works if you remember who they were, they have not deleted the
post, and they have not posted a thousand times since. Most of the time you remember the content, not the author.
X's advanced search operators have the same limit: they search all of X, not your saves.

## bookmarker press kit

Last updated 2 September 2026

bookmarker is a bookmark manager for iPhone and web that solves the thing every social app gets wrong: saved posts that pile up with no titles, no search and no order. Save from any app's share sheet and it's filed into a topic automatically — fifty topics, over six hundred subtopics — and fully searchable by title, tag, note or the account it came from. Bulk import turns an existing pile of Instagram, TikTok, X or YouTube saves (or a browser bookmarks file) into a sorted library in one step. It syncs between iPhone and this web app, asks for zero permissions, and carries no ads, no tracking and no third-party SDKs. Built by a solo developer using AI coding agents; launched 2 September 2026.

## bookmarker — Privacy Policy

Last updated 7 September 2026

bookmarker saves links you choose to save. This policy describes what is stored, where, and who can see it.

### What the app stores

For each link you save (a “bork”), bookmarker stores the URL, a title, the name of the account or site that posted it, which platform it came from, a topic and tags, any note you write, a thumbnail image when one is available, the date you saved it, and how many times you have opened it.

Some sites hand out thumbnail links that stop working after a few days. When you are signed in and a save carries one of those, our server fetches that thumbnail once and keeps a copy so your library keeps looking right. The copy is stored alongside your other data and is deleted with your account.

### Where it is stored

By default, on your device. If you never sign in, your library stays on your iPhone and we cannot see it.

If you sign in, your saved links and your email address are stored on our servers in the United States, so your library is backed up and available on your other devices. Access is restricted so only your account can read or write your data.

### Your email address

Signing in is how we verify who you are. We store your email address for the sole purpose of identifying your account and sending you a one-time sign-in code. There is no password. We do not send marketing email.

### What we do not do

- No advertising, and no advertising identifiers.

- No analytics or tracking SDKs in the iPhone app.

- No selling or sharing of your data with anyone.

- No tracking you across other apps or websites.

- No access to your contacts, photos, location, or microphone.

### Automatic filing

bookmarker sorts saved links into topics. Almost all of that happens on your device, offline, by matching words in the title and address.

When that is not enough to place a link and you are signed in, the app may ask a language model instead. In that case the link’s address, its title, the account that posted it, and any tags you typed are sent to our server and from there to a language model provider acting on our behalf, which returns a suggested topic. That provider does not use the request to train models. Your notes and your email address are never sent. If you are signed out, this never happens.

The web app at bookmarker.lol works the same way: it files your link in your browser first, offline, and only asks a language model when that comes back with nothing and you are signed in. The same four things are sent, and nothing else.

The suggestion is only a suggestion: it is shown to you and you can change it before saving.

### Library highlights

If you are signed in, the app can summarise what you have been saving lately. To do that, it sends the titles, topics and tags of up to 40 of your recent saves — never the links themselves, never your notes — to that same language model provider, which returns a short summary. This only runs inside the app for you; the result is not stored on our server and is not visible to anyone else. Signed out, this feature is off.

### Shared collections

You can group some of your saves into a collection and turn on a link for it. Until you do, a collection is private and nothing about it is visible to anyone else.

While the link is on, anyone who has it can open a page showing, for each bork you put in the collection: its link, its title, the account or site that posted it, its cover image and the topic it is filed under — plus the collection’s name, the note you wrote on it, and your display name. Nothing else. The page never shows your email address, the rest of your library, or the private notes you have written on those saves. It is not listed anywhere on bookmarker and asks search engines not to index it: the link is the only way to it, and it is not guessable.

People who open a shared page are not identified and are not asked to sign in. We record that the page was opened and how many items it had, so we know whether shared links are being used at all; no account, no profile and no cross-site tracking. The links on the page open the original post on the platform that hosts it, exactly as any other link would.

You can also give a link a time limit when you make it — one day or ten — and the page closes itself when that passes. Turning the link off, or deleting the collection, takes the page down within about a minute. If someone has already saved a copy of those links into their own library, that copy is theirs and stays with them — as it would if you had sent them the links in a message.

### Requests to other websites

When you save a link, the app may request that page directly from your device to read its title and preview image. That website therefore receives an ordinary web request from your device, as it would if you opened the link in a browser. bookmarker does not tell those sites who you are.

If you are signed in, our server may make the same kind of request — to read a page’s title and preview image, or to fetch a thumbnail that would otherwise expire. Those requests come from our server, identify themselves as bookmarker, and carry nothing about you.

To draw a small site icon next to each save, the app may also ask Google’s public favicon service for the icon of that site’s domain — the domain only, never the full link, and nothing about you.

### Deleting your data

Deleting a saved link removes it from your library. Deleting the app removes everything stored on your device.

To delete your account and everything stored on the server — your library, thumbnails and any feedback you sent while signed in — email hello@bookmarker.lol from your account’s email address, and it will be deleted within 30 days.

### The website

If you leave your email address on bookmarker.lol to hear about the beta or the launch, it is stored on our servers and used only to email you about bookmarker. No one else can see the list. To be removed, reply to any of those emails or write to hello@bookmarker.lol.

The website and web app use PostHog (hosted in the United States) for product analytics and session replay, so we can see where people get stuck and fix it. Replays mask everything you type. There are no advertising trackers, and none of this data is sold or shared.

If you send feedback from the Help tab, the message is stored on our servers together with what you were using at the time (web or mobile, screen size, browser) so bugs can be reproduced. If you are signed in it is tied to your account and deleted with it; if you are signed out, the email address you may leave is used only to reply to you. Feedback is read by the person who builds bookmarker and no one else.

If you import an export file from Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, Pinterest or your browser, that file is opened and read inside your own browser. It is never uploaded to us, and nor is anything in it that you do not import — the rest of an archive (your photos, messages, watch history) is not read and never leaves your computer. Only the saved links you confirm on the review screen are sent to your library: the address, a title, an author, the date it was originally saved, and the topic we filed it under. Which topic is worked out in your browser too; no imported link is sent to a model.

### Children

bookmarker is not directed at children under 13 and we do not knowingly collect their data.

### Changes

If this policy changes materially, the updated version will be posted here with a new date above.

### Contact

## bookmarker — Terms of Use

Last updated 31 August 2026

These terms cover the bookmarker app and the bookmarker web app at bookmarker.lol (together, "bookmarker"). By creating an account or using bookmarker, you agree to them.

### What bookmarker is

bookmarker lets you save links you choose to save, files them into topics, and makes them searchable. With an account, your saves are backed up and synced between your devices. bookmarker links out to the original pages; it does not host or reproduce their content.

### Your account

You sign in with your email address (via a one-time code) or a supported sign-in provider. Keep access to that email or provider account secure — it is how your account is protected. You must be at least 13 to use bookmarker. You can delete your account at any time from inside the app; that permanently removes your account and everything backed up on our servers.

### Your content

The links, notes, tags and topics you save are yours. You give us only the permission needed to store them, sync them between your devices, and show them back to you. We do not sell them, show them to anyone else, or use them for advertising — see the Privacy Policy for the details.

### Acceptable use

- Don't use bookmarker to store or distribute unlawful material.

- Don't probe, overload, resell or interfere with the service, or try to access anyone else's data.

- Don't use automated tools to bulk-fetch pages through bookmarker's preview service.

We may suspend or close accounts that break these rules.

### Automatic filing and summaries

Topic suggestions and library highlights are generated with the help of a language model and can be wrong. They are suggestions, not statements of fact, and you can always change how a save is filed.

### The service itself

bookmarker is provided "as is", free of charge, without warranties of any kind. We work to keep it available and your data safe, but we cannot promise uninterrupted service, and to the maximum extent permitted by law we are not liable for indirect or consequential damages, or losses caused by third-party sites and services a saved link points to. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited.

### Changes

If these terms change materially, the updated version will be posted here with a new date above. Continuing to use bookmarker after a change means you accept the updated terms. If we ever discontinue the service, we will give you a reasonable opportunity to export your saves.
